column1: ‘I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any subject.’
column2: “我要创办一所学府，让每个人都能在这里学习任何一门学科。”

column1: That was the founder’s motto for Cornell University, and it seems an apt characterization of the different university, also in the USA, where I currently teach philosophy.
column2: 这是康奈尔大学创办人的办学信条。我目前在美国另一所大学教授哲学，用这句话来描述那所学校，似乎也十分贴切。

column1: A student can prepare for a career in resort management, engineering, interior design, accounting, music, law enforcement, you name it.
column2: 学生可以为各种职业作准备：度假村管理、工程、室内设计、会计、音乐、执法……你能想到的都有。
column3: prepare for a career|为从业作准备
column8: you name it|你能想到的都有

column1: But what would the founders of these two institutions have thought of a course called ‘Arson for Profit’?
column2: 不过，这两所大学的创办人要是见到一门叫“纵火牟利”的课，会作何感想？

column1: I kid you not: we have it on the books.
column2: 我可没在开玩笑，我们的课程目录上真的有这门课。
column3: I kid you not|我可没开玩笑
column4: on the books|正式列在目录中

column1: Any undergraduates who have met the academic requirements can sign up for the course in our program in ‘fire science’.
column2: 凡是达到学业要求的本科生，都可以选修我们“消防科学”专业的这门课程。
column4: met the academic requirements|达到学业要求

column1: Naturally, the course is intended for prospective arson investigators, who can learn all the tricks of the trade for detecting whether a fire was deliberately set, discovering who did it, and establishing a chain of evidence for effective prosecution in a court of law.
column2: 这门课当然是为未来的纵火案调查员开设的。他们可以学习各种行内本领：判断火灾是否有人蓄意引发，查出是谁所为，并建立能让案件在法庭上得到有效起诉的证据链。
column6: tricks of the trade|行内的专门技巧

column1: But wouldn’t this also be the perfect course for prospective arsonists to sign up for?
column2: 然而，对打算纵火的人来说，这不也正是最合适报名的课程吗？
column3: perfect course|再合适不过的课程

column1: My point is not to criticize academic programs in fire science: they are highly welcome as part of the increasing professionalization of this and many other occupations.
column2: 我并不是想批评各校的消防科学专业。这个行业和其他许多职业都在逐步走向专业化，这类课程是其中备受欢迎的一环。

column1: However, it’s not unknown for a firefighter to torch a building.
column2: 不过，消防员纵火烧毁建筑物也并非没有先例。

column1: This example suggests how dishonest and illegal behavior, with the help of higher education, can creep into every aspect of public and business life.
column2: 这个例子说明，不诚实乃至违法的行为，如何能借助高等教育，悄悄渗入公共生活和商业生活的各个方面。

column1: I realized this anew when I was invited to speak before a class in marketing, which is another of our degree programs.
column2: 我受邀到一个市场营销班演讲时，再一次认识到了这一点。市场营销也是我们的学位课程之一。
column4: was invited to speak|受邀演讲

column1: The regular instructor is a colleague who appreciates the kind of ethical perspective I can bring as a philosopher.
column2: 平时任课的老师是我的同事，他很看重我作为哲学研究者能带来的伦理学视角。

column1: There are endless ways I could have approached this assignment, but I took my cue from the title of the course: ‘Principles of Marketing’.
column2: 我有无数种方式可以切入这次授课，但我从课名“市场营销原理”中得到了启发。
column6: took my cue from|从……获得启发
column7: Principles of Marketing|市场营销原理

column1: It made me think to ask the students, ‘Is marketing principled?’
column2: 于是我想到要问学生：“市场营销是讲道德原则的吗？”
column3: made me think to ask|让我想到要问

column1: After all, a subject matter can have principles in the sense of being codified, having rules, as with football or chess, without being principled in the sense of being ethical.
column2: 毕竟，一项活动可以有“原则”，也就是有明文规定的规则，像足球或国际象棋一样；可这并不意味着它“讲原则”，也就是符合道德。
column5: in the sense of|就……的意义而言

column1: Many of the students immediately assumed that the answer to my question about marketing principles was obvious: no.
column2: 许多学生立刻断定，我关于营销原则的这个问题，答案显而易见：不讲。

column1: Just look at the ways in which everything under the sun has been marketed; obviously it need not be done in a principled (=ethical) fashion.
column2: 只要看看世上形形色色的东西是如何被营销的就知道了。营销显然不一定要按讲原则（即合乎道德）的方式来做。
column3: everything under the sun|世上的一切东西

column1: Is that obvious?
column2: 果真如此显而易见吗？

column1: I made the suggestion, which may sound downright crazy in light of the evidence, that perhaps marketing is by definition principled.
column2: 我提出一个想法：从已有证据看，它也许听起来简直荒唐，但也许市场营销按其定义本来就应讲道德原则。

column1: My inspiration for this judgement is the philosopher Immanuel Kant, who argued that any body of knowledge consists of an end (or purpose) and a means.
column2: 我的这一判断受到了哲学家伊曼努尔·康德的启发。他主张，任何一套知识都包括目的和手段两个方面。

column1: Let us apply both the terms ‘means’ and ‘end’ to marketing.
column2: 让我们把“手段”和“目的”这两个概念都应用到市场营销中。

column1: The students have signed up for a course in order to learn how to market effectively.
column2: 学生选修这门课，是要学习如何有效地进行市场营销。

column1: But to what end?
column2: 可是，最终目的又是什么？
column3: to what end|为了什么目的

column1: There seem to be two main attitudes toward that question.
column2: 对这个问题，似乎主要有两种看法。

column1: One is that the answer is obvious: the purpose of marketing is to sell things and to make money.
column2: 一种看法认为答案很明显：营销的目的是卖东西、赚钱。

column1: The other attitude is that the purpose of marketing is irrelevant: Each person comes to the program and course with his or her own plans, and these need not even concern the acquisition of marketing expertise as such.
column2: 另一种看法认为，营销本身的目的无关紧要。每个人都带着自己的打算来读这个专业、选这门课，而个人的打算甚至未必与掌握营销专长本身有关。
column5: need not even concern|甚至未必与……有关

column1: My proposal, which I believe would also be Kant’s, is that neither of these attitudes captures the significance of the end to the means for marketing.
column2: 我的看法是，两种态度都没有抓住在营销中目的对于手段的意义。我相信，康德也会持这样的看法。

column1: A field of knowledge or a professional endeavor is defined by both the means and the end; hence both deserve scrutiny.
column2: 一个知识领域或一项专业工作都由其手段和目的共同界定，因此两者都值得仔细审视。

column1: Students need to study both how to achieve X, and also what X is.
column2: 学生既要研究如何实现X，也要研究X究竟是什么。
column5: what X is|目标X究竟是什么

column1: It is at this point that ‘Arson for Profit’ becomes supremely relevant.
column2: 正是在这一点上，“纵火牟利”这门课变得极为切题。

column1: That course is presumably all about means: how to detect and prosecute criminal activity.
column2: 可以推想，这门课全讲的是手段：如何查明犯罪活动，并依法提起公诉。

column1: It is therefore assumed that the end is good in an ethical sense.
column2: 因此，人们默认它的目的在伦理意义上是善的。
column6: in an ethical sense|在伦理意义上

column1: When I ask fire science students to articulate the end, or purpose, of their field, they eventually generalize to something like, “The safety and welfare of society,’ which seems right.
column2: 我请消防科学专业的学生明确说出他们这个领域的最终目标或目的。他们最后大致归纳为“社会的安全与福祉”，我觉得这说得对。

column1: As we have seen, someone could use the very same knowledge of means to achieve a much less noble end, such as personal profit via destructive, dangerous, reckless activity.
column2: 如前所述，同一个人也可以用完全相同的手段知识追求远不够高尚的目的，例如通过破坏性、危险又鲁莽的行为来谋取私利。

column1: But we would not call that firefighting.
column2: 但我们不会把那种行为称作消防。

column1: We have a separate word for it: arson.
column2: 我们另有一个词来称呼它：纵火。
column3: a separate word|另一个专门的词

column1: Similarly, if you employed the ‘principles of marketing’ in an unprincipled way, you would not be doing marketing.
column2: 同理，如果你以不讲道德的方式运用“营销原理”，那么你做的事就不能叫营销。
column6: in an unprincipled way|以不讲道德的方式

column1: We have another term for it: fraud.
column2: 对此我们另有一个词：欺诈。

column1: Kant gives the example of a doctor and a poisoner, who use the identical knowledge to achieve their divergent ends.
column2: 康德举了医生和投毒者的例子：两人运用完全相同的知识，却要达到截然不同的目的。

column1: We would say that one is practicing medicine, the other, murder.
column2: 我们会说，一个人在行医，另一个人在杀人。
